correctness.rationale: The normalized hollow symmetric Monge simplex has \(N=\binom n2\) explicit rectangle vertices. Inverting its triangular cumulative-coordinate map gives the two-index finite difference of the strictly upper-triangular entries. The intrinsic Frobenius metric is twice Euclidean squared length in those independent coordinates. Projecting the barycentric gradients onto the affine sum-zero plane yields the exact three-layer norms \(\sqrt2\,ab\) times \(2\), \(\sqrt{3-1/N}\), or \(\sqrt{1-1/N}\). The simplex facet-distance inequality gives the unique inball radius \(1/\sum g_{ab}\), and triangular sums yield the stated closed formula. Reconstructing its barycentric coordinates proves Toeplitz structure; discrete convexity proves strict triangle-inequality reversal; \(D_n=n^4/12+O(n^3)\) proves the uniform continuum scaling. A separate numerical inverse/LP check for \(3\le n\le10\) corroborates the calculations but is not an infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact, natural Euclidean Chebyshev center for the normalized hollow symmetric Monge simplex of transportation-cost matrices, previously studied mainly for its face structure and volume. The uniquely selected center is Toeplitz, violates every ordered triangle inequality strictly, and tends uniformly to the normalized squared-distance transport kernel \(6(s-t)^2\). These are structural geometric facts rather than a textbook application of a generic simplex formula. The inradius leading constant \(6\sqrt2\) differs from the published nonsymmetric square Monge case.
